text:
talia: quick RFC follow-up — i'm proposing a compact-pipeline quarantine flow for air-gapped upgrades. gist: pull compact manifests first, run fast checks, then stream payloads per-component only when verified. keeps disk low and reduces churn.

ryan: sounds useful. main downside is state complexity — partial activations increase operator logic.

mei: agree. proposal: operator stores a simple ActivationPlan with per-component markers (PULLED, QUARANTINED, VERIFIED, ACTIVATING, ACTIVE). only flip global activation marker on policy.

omar: sidecar vs builtin verifier? sidecar favoured for KMS and HSM isolation.

talia: +1 sidecar. minimal API: VerifyManifest(manifest_hash, component_id, activation_key) -> {VERIFIED|REJECT|RETRY, code}. operator stays keyless.

ryan: GC defaults? we must avoid SSD overfill on tiny nodes.

talia: defaults: ttl=48h, max_items=4, max_bytes=1GB. eviction LRU prefer non-activated components. expose metrics: quarantine_items, quarantine_bytes, quarantine_evictions.

mei: offline-escrow for true airgap? admin uploads escrow blob once, console requires explicit ack. verifier uses local crypto checks. rotation via signed rotation manifest or maintenance-mode approval.

omar: failure semantics? transient -> retries; persistent -> QUARANTINED-REJECT and operator emits an event with remediation link.

ryan: rollout plan? dry-run first where verifier returns simulated rejects but operator does not change state. then small canary with short grace window (5m).
